**Supplerende indikator: Mortalitet** (Supplementary Indicator: Mortality) is a clinical outcome metric utilized within the [[atrieflimren-i-danmark|Atrieflimren i Danmark]] (AFDK) regional quality development program, which is administered by the Danish Healthcare Quality Programme (Sundhedsvæsenets Kvalitetsinstitut) [^src1]. As a supplementary indicator, it is designed to measure the proportion of prevalent patients with atrial fibrillation who die during a given reporting period, thereby contributing to the broader assessment of treatment quality and healthcare system performance [^src1].

This specific outcome is formally tracked by [[indikator-9|Indikator 9]], which calculates the share of prevalent patients with an atrial fibrillation diagnosis who die within the reporting timeframe [^src1]. The mortality data is reported across national, regional, and health cluster levels, and is presented alongside confidence intervals to provide statistical context [^src1]. The underlying data is derived from linkage with the Danish Civil Registration System (CPR register) and is strictly limited to patients who possess a Danish CPR number and reside in the country [^src1]. 

When interpreting this indicator, the AFDK reports highlight a significant methodological limitation: the reported mortality proportions are unadjusted [^src1]. Consequently, there is a risk of case-mix effects, which makes direct comparisons between different healthcare units problematic unless the data is further adjusted for underlying demographic and clinical factors [^src1].
